Description - POST /file/

Stores one file using an UploadToken ticket.

URL. The client first builds http://<server>/file/?key=..&stamp=..&folderId=..&fileName=..[&imageSize=WxH][&locale=..] and then posts to scheme://host/path, i.e. without the query (the server does not need it).

Body. Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=!CHB<stamp> with the client's own part framing (see UploadMultipartBody): parts chomik_id, folder_id, key, time, [resume_from], [thumbnail parts], client, locale, file. With the exact client framing the stored file is byte-identical (verified by SHA-256 after download).

Transport. With [proto-box] direct-upload=true (default) the client uses a raw socket (POST <path> HTTP/1.0, Host, Content-Length); otherwise QNetworkAccessManager. Captures used HTTP/1.1 with Content-Length; no difference observed. Network errors are retried (send-retry-count 5; delay [network] send-retry-delay, application default 15 s, clamped 1..300 s; the INI line upload-retry-delay = 15 is not read).

Headers. Besides Content-Type and Content-Length ChomikBox sets no header. Over the default raw-socket transport the Qt 4.8.5 defaults (User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0, …) presumably do not apply (Inferred); over QNetworkAccessManager they do (see "SOAP wire format" in info.description).

Forced file server. The start-up switch or single-instance pipe command --file-server <host> makes the client post every upload, upload key included, and every resume check to that host instead of the UploadToken server (effect Inferred, C-08).

Generators beware. The part header lines are fixed (see UploadMultipartBody x-part-headers): text parts name="…" + Content-Type: text/plain, thumbnails Content-Type: image/jpeg, and the file part only name="file"; filename="…" with no Content-Type. A default OpenAPI multipart serialiser (Content-Disposition, Content-Type per part) corrupts the stored file.

Reply. XML <resp res="1" fileid="…"/> served as text/html; res != 1 is an error with errorMessage.

Notes

  • The client tag is %1-%2 (Inferred ChomikBox-2.0.8.2) with boundary !CHB<stamp>, as in 5 of 6 captures. The server also accepts chomikbox-2.0.8.2 and the bare boundary !CHB (bare-chb-boundary). Not a client-vs-live discrepancy.

Request - body and examples

Body required.

Upload body. The captured examples show the body only; their descriptions give the request line and headers (Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=!CHB…).

Body multipart/mixed

Schema

Schema UploadMultipartBody: parts in wire order.

Upload body as built by the client, in this order. Non-standard framing: each part starts with the line name="<name>"[; filename="<name>"] instead of a Content-Disposition header; text parts then carry Content-Type: text/plain, thumbnails Content-Type: image/jpeg, and the file part has no Content-Type line. The server parses positionally (name line, one more header line, content); adding a Content-Type to the file part corrupts the stored file. Boundary !CHB<stamp>; the bare !CHB is accepted too.

  • part chomik_id integer (int32) required

    Account (hamster) id from AuthResult.

  • part folder_id integer (int32) required

    Target folder id (the folderId of the UploadToken call).

  • part key string required

    UploadToken key. A forged key gives res="-42" errorMessage="Bad token".

  • part time string required

    UploadToken stamp.

  • part resume_from integer (int64) optional

    Byte offset to continue from; only sent when resuming (from the resume check file_size). The file part then contains the bytes from this offset.

  • part width integer optional

    Image width (sent with client-generated thumbnails).

  • part height integer optional

    Image height.

  • part th_width integer optional

    Thumbnail width (default thumbnail 160x120).

  • part th_height integer optional

    Thumbnail height.

  • part thumb string · image/jpeg optional

    JPEG thumbnail (quality thumb-quality 82), followed by CRLF.

  • part medthumb string · image/jpeg optional

    Medium JPEG thumbnail; only when its size differs from thumb.

  • part client string optional

    Client tag %1-%2 = base.ini title + version (Inferred ChomikBox-2.0.8.2); 5 of 6 captures send ChomikBox-2.0.8.2. Not validated by the server: chomikbox-2.0.8.2 is accepted too (bare-chb-boundary).

  • part locale string optional

    UploadToken locale, when non-empty.

  • part file string required

    Raw file bytes (from resume_from if resuming), filename= = the UploadToken fileName (UTF-8). The part has no Content-Type line (header block = exactly name="file"; filename="<name>"); there is deliberately no contentMediaType here because an OAS-driven generator would emit it as a header, and Content-Type: application/octet-stream makes the server store a leading \r\n. Followed by \r\n--!CHB<stamp>--\r\n.

Part header lines (x-part-headers)

Exact header lines of each part, in order, between the delimiter line --!CHB<stamp> and the blank line. OpenAPI cannot express a part without Content-Type or a part named without Content-Disposition, so generators must special-case this body. tools/validate.mjs checks every multipart example against this table.

Pattern for text parts: name="<part>"
Content-Type: text/plain

Responses - 200, 4XX

200

Upload reply (XML in a text/html; charset=utf-8 response). Check res.

Schema text/html

Schema UploadReply, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <resp> object required UploadReply no namespace

    Reply of the upload server. Root element must be resp; res="1" is success, anything else is a server error (code 1), HTTP >= 400 is code 1, non-XML is code 2 (xml-parse-error). Served as text/html; charset=utf-8 by Microsoft-HTTPAPI/2.0 despite being XML. Live: success carries only res and fileid; the filename/folderid attributes read by the client are not sent.

    • @res integer required

      Result code: 1 = stored; negative = error (observed -42 "Bad token").

    • @fileid integer (int64) optional

      Id of the stored file (read by the client as i64).

    • @filename string optional

      Read by the client but never sent by the service.

    • @folderid integer optional

      Read by the client (compared with the local folder, warning "folder mistatch!") but never sent by the service.

    • @errorMessage string optional

      Error text for res != 1, shown in the uploader.

4XX

Not observed live. Client behaviour: any HTTP status >= 400 is treated as a server error (code 1) and the upload is retried per send-retry-count.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • The reply has only res and fileid; the client also reads filename and folderid, which are never sent.

Security notes - findings that concern POST /file/

  • C-01 High All client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it.
  • C-08 Low The single-instance named pipe and the chomik:// scheme accept commands (-d<url>, -u, -p) from any local process or web link. The pipe also accepts --file-server <host>, which redirects all uploads and resume checks, upload keys included, to that host (command Observed; effect Inferred, the link to the upload path was not fully confirmed).

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
